===========================================================
README - Setting up C/C++ Development in VS Code (Windows)
===========================================================

This guide covers:
1. Installing VS Code Community Edition
2. Installing compiler toolchain (MSYS2 + MinGW-w64)
3. Configuring environment
4. Creating a simple HelloWorld project with CMake
5. Extending to a multi-file project with subdirectories

-----------------------------------------------------------
1. Install VS Code Community Edition
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Download from https://code.visualstudio.com/
- Run installer, keep defaults unless you prefer custom paths.

-----------------------------------------------------------
2. Install C/C++ Extension
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Open VS Code.
- Press Ctrl+Shift+X → Extensions.
- Search for "C/C++" (Microsoft) → Install.
- Optional: Install "CMake Tools" extension for easier integration.

-----------------------------------------------------------
3. Install Compiler (MSYS2 + MinGW-w64)
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Download MSYS2 from https://www.msys2.org
- Install to C:\msys64
- Open MSYS2 terminal and run:
    pacman -Syu
    pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc gdb make cmake
- Add C:\msys64\mingw64\bin to your Windows PATH.
- Verify installation:
    g++ --version
    gdb --version
    cmake --version

-----------------------------------------------------------
4. Simple HelloWorld Project
-----------------------------------------------------------

Project Structure:
HelloWorld/
├── main.cpp
├── CMakeLists.txt
└── .vscode/
    ├── tasks.json
    └── launch.json

main.cpp:
-----------------------------------
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    cout << "Hello, World!" << endl;
    return 0;
}
-----------------------------------

CMakeLists.txt:
-----------------------------------
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.10)
project(HelloWorld LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

add_executable(helloworld main.cpp)
-----------------------------------

.vscode/tasks.json:
-----------------------------------
{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "label": "cmake build",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "cmake",
      "args": ["--build", "build"],
      "group": { "kind": "build", "isDefault": true }
    }
  ]
}
-----------------------------------

.vscode/launch.json:
-----------------------------------
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "name": "Debug HelloWorld",
      "type": "cppdbg",
      "request": "launch",
      "program": "${workspaceFolder}/build/helloworld.exe",
      "cwd": "${workspaceFolder}",
      "stopAtEntry": false,
      "externalConsole": true,
      "MIMode": "gdb",
      "miDebuggerPath": "gdb.exe"
    }
  ]
}
-----------------------------------

Build & Run:
    cmake -S . -B build
    cmake --build build
    ./build/helloworld.exe

-----------------------------------------------------------
5. Complex Project with Subdirectories
-----------------------------------------------------------

Project Structure:
ComplexProject/
├── CMakeLists.txt
├── src/
│   ├── main.cpp
│   └── CMakeLists.txt
├── lib/
│   ├── helper.c
│   ├── helper.h
│   └── CMakeLists.txt
└── .vscode/
    ├── tasks.json
    └── launch.json

src/main.cpp:
-----------------------------------
#include <iostream>
#include "helper.h"

int main() {
    std::cout << "Complex Project!" << std::endl;
    print_message("Hello from C helper!");
    return 0;
}
-----------------------------------

lib/helper.c:
-----------------------------------
#include "helper.h"
#include <stdio.h>

void print_message(const char* msg) {
    printf("%s\n", msg);
}
-----------------------------------

lib/helper.h:
-----------------------------------
#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

void print_message(const char* msg);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
-----------------------------------

Top-level CMakeLists.txt:
-----------------------------------
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.10)
project(ComplexProject LANGUAGES C CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

add_subdirectory(lib)
add_subdirectory(src)
-----------------------------------

src/CMakeLists.txt:
-----------------------------------
add_executable(complex main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(complex helper)
-----------------------------------

lib/CMakeLists.txt:
-----------------------------------
add_library(helper helper.c)
-----------------------------------

.vscode/tasks.json:
-----------------------------------
{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "label": "cmake build",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "cmake",
      "args": ["--build", "build"],
      "group": { "kind": "build", "isDefault": true }
    }
  ]
}
-----------------------------------

.vscode/launch.json:
-----------------------------------
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "name": "Debug ComplexProject",
      "type": "cppdbg",
      "request": "launch",
      "program": "${workspaceFolder}/build/src/complex.exe",
      "cwd": "${workspaceFolder}",
      "stopAtEntry": false,
      "externalConsole": true,
      "MIMode": "gdb",
      "miDebuggerPath": "gdb.exe"
    }
  ]
}
-----------------------------------

Build & Run:
    cmake -S . -B build
    cmake --build build
    ./build/src/complex.exe

-----------------------------------------------------------
6. Workflow Summary
-----------------------------------------------------------
1. Install VS Code + C/C++ extension.
2. Install MSYS2 → GCC, GDB, CMake.
3. Add compiler to PATH.
4. Create project folder with source files.
5. Write CMakeLists.txt (simple or multi-directory).
6. Configure build:
    cmake -S . -B build
    cmake --build build
7. Run executable.
8. Debug with VS Code (F5).

-----------------------------------------------------------
Tips for Future Projects
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Use CMake for scalability (handles many files, subdirectories).
- Use tasks.json for builds and launch.json for debugging.
- Always link with g++ when mixing C and C++.
- Use extern "C" in headers for interoperability.
- Install CMake Tools extension for one-click configure/build/debug.
